subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Early Pregnancy Signs: Hegar, Chadwick and Goodell

steps.tx: Softening and compressibility of the lower uterine segment on bimanual examination is the **Hegar sign**. It appears at six to eight weeks as the isthmus softens under hormonal influence. Modern practice relies on urine testing and ultrasound instead. Osiander sign, a stronger vaginal artery pulse felt at eight weeks, belongs to the same group of soft signs.
steps.say: The Hegar sign softens the lower uterine segment at six to eight weeks of pregnancy.

steps.tx: Bluish discoloration of the vagina and cervix from increased vascularity is the **Chadwick sign**. It appears around eight to twelve weeks of pregnancy. Other causes of pelvic congestion can mimic it, so it stays suggestive rather than diagnostic. Palmer sign describes regular rhythmic contractions of the early pregnant uterus felt on bimanual examination.
steps.say: The Chadwick sign blues the vagina from vascularity around eight to twelve weeks.

steps.tx: Softening of the cervix to the consistency of lips is the **Goodell sign**. The non pregnant cervix feels like the tip of the nose by comparison. It develops by about six weeks under progesterone influence. Chadwick sign was described in 1886 and fades in value once a urine test can answer the question in two minutes.
steps.say: The Goodell sign softens the cervix to lip consistency by about six weeks.

steps.tx: A two minute urine test replaced a shelf of clinical signs for good reason. The **urine pregnancy test** detects hCG with accuracy that physical signs like cervix softening never matched, and it works before most signs appear. Its limits still matter: very early testing, dilute urine and rare variants can mislead. Knowing what the test measures keeps a negative result in perspective when the clinical story strongly suggests pregnancy.
steps.say: Urine tests detect hCG far more reliably than physical pregnancy signs. Very early or dilute testing can still mislead, so context matters.

vis.alt: Image of a urine pregnancy test showing a positive result.
vis.caption: A urine pregnancy test device is shown with a positive result window. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Every modern pregnancy diagnosis starts with a **urine pregnancy test** detecting hCG. It turns positive around the missed period and is highly accurate when performed correctly. Very early testing before the missed period can falsely reassure. False negatives follow very dilute urine, so a first morning sample is used when the period is only just missed.
steps.say: Urine pregnancy tests detect hCG and turn positive around the missed period.

steps.tx: Quantitative blood measurement of the hormone is **beta-hCG** testing. Serial values track viability, rising by at least half in forty eight hours in most healthy early pregnancies. Ultrasound location matters more than any single value. Below the discriminatory zone of about 1500 to 2000 international units per litre, a normal sac may simply be too early to see on transvaginal scan.
steps.say: Beta-hCG serial values track viability, rising by half in forty eight hours when healthy.

steps.tx: Irregular contractions of the pregnant uterus felt on examination are **Braxton Hicks** precursors in early form, while palpable intermittent painless contractions appear later. They never dilate the cervix. Confusing them with true labour is common near term. Contractions that come at irregular intervals, stay mild and ease with rest or hydration fit Braxton Hicks rather than labour.
steps.say: Painless Braxton Hicks contractions never dilate the cervix, unlike true labour.

steps.tx: The yolk sac confirms location in the first weeks, whereas later visits are dominated by uterine tightenings that are not labour. Irregular contractions felt on examination are early **Braxton Hicks** activity, and palpable intermittent painless contractions appear as pregnancy advances. They never dilate the cervix. Near term they are often mistaken for true labour. Contractions at uneven intervals that stay mild and ease with rest or hydration fit this pattern. The early intrauterine sac is a first trimester finding and does not predict how those later painless tightenings will behave.
steps.say: Braxton Hicks contractions are intermittent and painless, occur at irregular intervals, stay mild, and ease with rest or hydration. They do not open the cervix. Near term they are often mistaken for labour, which is regular and progressive rather than relieved by simple rest.

vis.alt: A transvaginal ultrasound in the sixth week shows an intrauterine gestational sac containing a round yolk sac.
vis.caption: The sac lies within the decidua and holds a distinct round yolk sac, confirming an early pregnancy inside the uterus. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Enlargement of the uterus asymmetric at the implantation site is the **Piskacek sign**. One cornu bulges where the embryo implanted in early weeks. It disappears as the sac grows to fill the cavity. It can be mistaken for a fibroid on palpation, and an ultrasound resolves the doubt in minutes.
steps.say: The Piskacek sign bulges one cornu at the implantation site in early weeks.

steps.tx: Definitive confirmation of intrauterine pregnancy needs ultrasound showing a **gestational sac with yolk sac**. This excludes ectopic pregnancy in most symptomatic cases. A sac without yolk or embryo at expected sizes needs interval rescan. Seeing a yolk sac inside the sac separates a true pregnancy sac from the fluid collection, a pseudosac, sometimes seen in ectopic pregnancy.
steps.say: Ultrasound showing sac with yolk sac confirms intrauterine pregnancy and excludes most ectopics.

vis.alt: Obstetric ultrasound showing intrauterine gestational sac with double decidual sign and yolk sac.
vis.caption: Obstetric ultrasound showing intrauterine gestational sac with double decidual sign and yolk sac. Early pregnancy ultrasound showing gestational sac and yolk sac. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Symptoms of pregnancy including amenorrhoea, nausea and breast tenderness are called **presumptive symptoms**. They prompt testing but never confirm pregnancy alone. Objective confirmation always follows with test and scan. Quickening, first fetal movements felt at 18 to 20 weeks in a first pregnancy, is the presumptive symptom patients most often quote.
steps.say: Presumptive symptoms prompt testing but objective confirmation always follows.
